stem: Bihar state is situated between the following longitudes
expl: Bihar State lies between 83°19′50″E to 88°17′40″E longitudes. Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer.

stem: The total geographical area of Bihar State is:

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: After the formation of Jharkhand State on 15 November 2000, Bihar’s present area is 94,163 sq km. This is about 2.86% of India’s total area. In terms of area, it stands at 13th position overall among the States and Union Territories of India (after including the Union Territory of Ladakh).

stem: Local time of Patna is—

options.label: c
options.text: The same as Indian Standard Time.

options.label: d
options.text: Not related to Indian Standard Time.

expl: Patna’s standard time is determined by Indian Standard Time (IST). India’s standard time is based on 82°30′E longitude, which passes through Mirzapur. India’s standard time is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), whereas Patna’s local time is ahead of IST, because Patna is located at 85°1′E longitude.

stem: Most of Bihar comes under which of the following climate type?
expl: Most of Bihar falls under Subtropical monsoon climate, but in the south-eastern part of the State, some districts—such as Jamui, Banka, Munger, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Sheikhpura (entire parts) and some parts of Bhagalpur, Saharsa and Begusarai—fall under tropical savanna climate.

stem: According to Koppen's Climate Classification, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar are in which climate Category?

options.label: e
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: According to the India Meteorological Department, under Köppen’s climate classification scheme, the districts located in the south-eastern part of Bihar State, namely Jamui, Banka, Munger, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Sheikhpura (entire parts) and some parts of Bhagalpur, Saharsa and Begusarai fall under Aw type climatic region, whereas the remaining parts of the State fall under Cwa type climatic region. According to NCERT, the Cwg climatic condition extends over the Gangetic Plains, eastern Rajasthan, northern Madhya Pradesh and most parts of north-eastern India. Since both Uttar Pradesh and Bihar are included in the Gangetic Plains, Cwg climatic condition is found in both the States. On this basis, the Bihar Public Service Commission considered option (b) as the correct answer.

stem: According to Köppen's climate classification, the climate of North Bihar can be represented by which of the following?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: According to the India Meteorological Department, under Köppen’s climate classification scheme, the districts located in the south-eastern part of Bihar State, namely Jamui, Banka, Munger, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Sheikhpura (entire parts) and some parts of Bhagalpur, Saharsa and Begusarai fall under Aw type climatic region, whereas the remaining parts of the State fall under Cwa type climatic region. According to NCERT, the Cwg climatic condition extends over the Gangetic Plains, eastern Rajasthan, northern Madhya Pradesh and most parts of north-eastern India. Since both Uttar Pradesh and Bihar are included in the Gangetic Plains, Cwg climatic condition is found in both the States. On this basis, the Bihar Public Service Commission considered option (b) as the correct answer.

stem: According to Thornthwaite's scheme, what type of climate does eastern Bihar have?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: According to Thornthwaite’s scheme, the climate of Eastern Bihar is mainly of the C type. However, due to variations in the distribution of rainfall within the region, both dry sub-humid (C1) and moist sub-humid (C) sub-types are found. The northern and north-eastern districts of Eastern Bihar (Purnia, Araria, Kishanganj, etc.) fall under the C category because of higher rainfall, whereas the south-western part (Bhagalpur, etc.) comes under the C1 category due to comparatively lower rainfall. The Bihar Public Service Commission has considered option (a) as the correct answer in its answer key.

stem: According to R. L. Singh’s classification scheme, Bihar falls under which type of climatic region?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: According to R. L. Singh’s classification scheme, Bihar falls under the sub-humid transitional type of climatic region. R. L. Singh presented his climatic divisions in the year 1971. On the basis of the temperature conditions of the hottest and coldest months and the average annual rainfall, he divided the country into 10 climatic divisions.

stem: Chotanagpur Plateau is—
expl: In the Chotanagpur Plateau, a sequence of plateaus of different elevations is found. In the middle-western part lies the Pat land, whose maximum height is about 1100 m. Steps or terraces are found in all directions of this plateau, and steep slopes occur widely. Therefore, it is a cuesta.

stem: The parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar are included in which of the following plains?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: Parts of Eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar are included in the Middle Ganga Plain.

stem: The plains of Magadha and Anga are parts of which of the following?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Anga and Magadha were among the sixteen Mahajanapadas. The capital of the Anga Mahajanapada was Champa. It lay within the present-day districts of Munger and Bhagalpur in Bihar. The capital of Magadha was Girivraja (Rajgriha), later shifted to Pataliputra. Both Mahajanapadas were located within the Middle Ganga Plain.

stem: Munger Hilly region is a part of which of the following physiographic region ?
expl: The Munger hilly region is a part of the southern hilly region of the state of Bihar. It is an extension of the Chotanagpur Plateau.

stem: Which of the following landforms occupy the North-Western parts of Bihar state?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The north-western part of Bihar state is bounded by the Someshwar Range. The Someshwar Range and the Dun Range are parts of the Outer Himalayan Range.

stem: Someshwar range of Bihar is-
expl: The Sumeshwar (Someshwar) Range of Bihar and the Shivalik Range were formed mainly during the Pleistocene period. Therefore, it is younger than all the three hills mentioned above.

stem:
Correctly match List-I (Agro-climatic zones) with List-II (Percentage of Bihar's Area) and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists :
List-I List-II (Agro-climatic zones) (Percentage of Bihar's area)
A. North and North- 1. 29.87% Eastern Bihar Plains
B. South Bihar Plains 2. 23.71%
C. Chhota Nagpur Plateau 3. 26.14%
D. Chhota Nagpur Hills 4. 20.28%
Code : A B C D
expl: With reference to undivided Bihar, option (b) was the correct answer. Geographically, Bihar is divided into three regions— Sub-Himalayan foothill region, Indo-Gangetic plains, and Southern plateau region. The Sub-Himalayan foothill region extends over the northern part of Bihar. Some small hills such as the Someshwar and Doon hills are found here. To its south lies the Terai region, which is a marshy and sparsely populated belt. The river Ganga divides the Gangetic plains of Bihar into two parts—North and South.

stem: Which of the following pairs does not correspond to the south Ganga region of Bihar?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: In Bihar, the Southern Ganga Plains constitute about 43.42 percent of the total geographical area of the state. Therefore, Patna–Munger and Gaya–Arwal districts fall in the Southern Ganga region, whereas Vaishali lies in the Northern Ganga region.

stem: In which one of the following pairs of Administrative Divisions of Bihar, the Ganga river does not flow?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: During its course, the river Ganga flows through the Darbhanga–Munger, Purnea–Bhagalpur, and Tirhut–Saran administrative divisions. It does not flow through the Kosi– Magadh administrative division. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

stem: In Bihar, the terms Balsundari, Tal, Karail and Balthar are used for which of the following?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: In Bihar, the terms Balsundari, Tal, Karail, and Balthar are used for soil. Various types of soils are found in the state. Alluvial soil covers the largest area in Bihar. In the Kaimur region, Balthar soil (sandy, calcareous, yellow) is found, while Khadar soil is mainly found in Muzaffarpur, Katihar, Saharsa, and Darbhanga. Terai soil is mainly found in East Champaran and West Champaran districts; Bangar soil in Patna and Rohtas districts; Balsundari soil in Saharsa, East Champaran, and West Champaran districts; and marshy soil is found in the north-western corner of Bihar.

stem: In which of the following district-pairs is the reserve of old alluvial soil found in Bihar?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The reserve of old alluvial soil (Bangar) is found mainly in Purnea and Patna districts among the districts mentioned in the question.

stem: Piedmont Swamp Soil is found only in which one of the following districts of Bihar?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Three major types of soils are found in Bihar— (i) Piedmont swamp soil, found in the north-western part of West Champaran district. (ii) Terai soil, found in the northern part of the state along the Nepal border. (iii) Gangetic alluvial soil—the plains of Bihar are covered with Gangetic alluvium (both new and old).

stem: Most of the area of Bihar is covered with -

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/Above more than one

expl: Most of Bihar is covered with alluvial (Kachhari) soil.

stem: Which one of the following parts of Bihar is geologically older in age relatively?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Kharagpur Hills consist of Pre-Cambrian/Proterozoic rocks of the Munger–Rajgir range, whereas the Rohtas Plateau belongs to the Vindhyan sequence; the North-Western Hills are a part of the Shivalik Himalaya (Upper Tertiary to Early Quaternary), and the North Ganga Plain is the newest.

stem:
The geographical structure of Bihar is made up of rock systems. Match the rock systems with their descriptions—
A. Dharwar rock system 1. Formed by rapid deposition of sediments by Himalayan and Peninsular rivers
B. Vindhyan rock system 2. Can be found in West Champaran district
C. Quaternary rock system 3. A part of the oldest Archean rock system
D. Tertiary rock system 4. Sandstone, limestone, dolomite, quartzite and shale are the main components of this rock system Use the code given below and choose the correct answer. A B C D
expl: The correct matching is as follows— Dharwar rock system — A part of the oldest Archean Vindhyan rock system — Sandstone, limestone, Quaternary rock system — Formed by rapid deposition Tertiary rock system — Can be found in West

stem: Which of the following districts does not have a Dharwar geological structure?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In Bihar, districts with Dharwar stratigraphic structure lie in south-eastern Bihar. These include Munger, Nawada and Jamui, whereas Rohtas is a part of south-western Bihar. Vindhyan sequence rocks are found in this region. In Bihar, Vindhyan sequence rocks occur in the Kaimur region and the Son river valley (Rohtas).

stem: Which of the following physiographic divisions of Bihar does not share its boundary with Jharkhand?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The geomorphological division “Mithila Plain” of Bihar does not share its boundary with Jharkhand, whereas the Ganga– Son Divide, Anga Plain and Magadha Plain do share a boundary with Jharkhand.

stem: The percentage of land area of old Bihar that forms the State of Jharkhand is –
expl: Before the formation of Jharkhand, the total area of undivided Bihar was 173,877 sq. km. Out of this, 79,714 sq. km. area was used for the formation of the state of Jharkhand on 15 November, 2000. Hence, Jharkhand was formed by taking about 45.84% of the land of old Bihar; therefore, the nearest option (b) is correct. At present, the total area of Bihar is 94,163 sq. km.

stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the various geographical aspects of Bihar –
I. Agriculture contributes nearly 67 per cent to Bihar's domestic product.
II. Silk industry in Bihar provides self-employment to over 1,50,000 people
III. About 47 lakh acres of land in Bihar get flooded every year, while 10 lakh acres remain permanently waterlogged.
IV. 85 to 90 percent of Bihar's rural households own less than 5 acres of land each.
Which of these statements are correct?
expl: At the time of the question, option (c) was the correct answer. In 2022–23 (provisional) and 2023–24 (quick estimate), the share of agriculture, forestry and fishing in Bihar’s gross state value added was 20.2 percent and 19.5 percent respectively. In 2024–25 (up to January 2025), the estimated number of persons employed in Bihar’s silk sector was 0.24 lakh. In 2023, about 2.914 million hectares area in Bihar was affected by floods.

stem: Which soil is mostly found in Muzaffarpur, Darbhanga and Champaran districts?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In Darbhanga and Muzaffarpur districts, new alluvial soil (Khadar) is found. New alluvial soil (Khadar) is formed due to the deposition of debris/silt brought every year by the flood water of rivers. In East Champaran and West Champaran districts of Bihar, along with new alluvial soil (Khadar), Terai soil and Balsundari soil are also found.

stem: Kaimur Plateau is famous for –

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Kaimur Plateau is famous for limestone. The Kaimur Plateau is located in Rohtas and Kaimur districts. This plateau is made up of shale, limestone and sandstone. On the basis of the limestone of this plateau, there is a cement industry at Banjari.

stem: North Bihar is famous for –
expl: 73.63 percent of the area of North Bihar is vulnerable to floods. Due to floods every year in this region, crops and public life get disrupted.

stem: Which of the following cities is located in the easternmost part of Bihar?
expl: Katihar is situated in the easternmost part of Bihar. To the south of Katihar lie Bhagalpur and Sahibganj district of Jharkhand; to the east lies Malda district of West Bengal; to the north lies Dinajpur district; and to the north and west lies Purnia.

stem: Brahmayoni Hill is located in which district of Bihar?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Brahmayoni Hill is a sacred hill located in Gaya district of Bihar. It is mentioned in the Mahabharata, Buddhist inscriptions, etc. Gaya district is situated on the bank of the Phalgu River.

stem: Which city of Bihar is surrounded by five hills?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Rajgir city of Bihar is surrounded by five hills, which is also mentioned in various texts including the Mahabharata. The hills of Rajgir are world-famous. The names of these five hills are Vipulagiri (Vipulachal), Ratnagiri, Udaygiri, Swarnagiri and Vaibhavgiri (Vaibhargiri). Gaya is surrounded on three sides by small rocky hills, named—Mangala-Gauri, Shring Sthan, Ramshila and Brahmayoni.

stem: The number of Indian states touching the boundary of Bihar is –
expl: At the time of the question, undivided Bihar shared its boundary with four states (Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha, and West Bengal). After the bifurcation on 15 November 2000, the Indian states touching Bihar’s boundary are Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, and Jharkhand.

stem: Which of the following districts of Bihar does not share border with Nepal?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Bihar shares an international boundary of 729 km with Nepal. Seven districts of Bihar share a boundary with Nepal— Sitamarhi, Kishanganj, Araria, Supaul, Madhubani, East Champaran, and West Champaran.

stem: After the formation of Jharkhand how many districts were left with Bihar? (Nearest figure)
expl: After the formation of Jharkhand, 37 districts remained in Bihar. Before the formation of Jharkhand, Bihar had 55 districts. Eighteen districts of Bihar went to the newly formed state of Jharkhand. At present, Bihar has 38 districts. The 38th district, “Arwal”, was created in August 2001 by bifurcating Jehanabad.

stem: By how many districts of Bihar was Patna district bounded till July 2018?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: At present, Patna district shares its boundary with 9 districts, namely—Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Samastipur, Begusarai, Lakhisarai, Nalanda, Jehanabad, and Arwal.

stem: Which of the following districts of Bihar transferred some of its areas to West Bengal?
expl: During the reorganization of states in 1956, most parts of Purulia located in the then Manbhum district of undivided Bihar (except Patamda police station) and some parts of Purnia were transferred to West Bengal.

stem:
Forests of Chhotanagpur are –
(i) Evergreen (ii) Deciduous
(iii) Savanna (iv) Thorny
Select your answer out of the following codes –

options.label: a
options.text: i and ii both are true

options.label: c
options.text: ii and iii both are true

expl: The forests of the Chhotanagpur region mainly consist of deciduous vegetation, in which mahua, khair, semal, shisham, mango, and banyan are prominent. Along with this, savanna-type forests are also found here. The presence of scattered trees in grassland (scrub) areas is a characteristic feature of savanna-type forests.

stem: The percent of the total geographical area of Bihar covered by forests is-
expl: During the period of the question, option (a) was the correct answer. According to the India State of Forest Report (ISFR), 2023, forest cover in Bihar is 8% (7,532.45 sq km) and tree cover is 2.52% (2,370.21 sq km) of the total geographical area (94,163 sq km). Thus, as per the updated status, the total forest cover and tree cover together account for 10.52% (9,902.66 sq km) of the state’s area.

stem: What is the percentage of all types of forest area to the total geographical area of Bihar State?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: According to the India State of Forest Report, 2019, the forest area in Bihar was 7.84 percent of the total geographical area. According to the India State of Forest Report, 2023, the forest area in Bihar is recorded at approximately 8 percent of the total geographical area.

stem: Among the following districts, which one has the larger area under dense deciduous forest cover?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: At the time of the question as well as at present, West Champaran has the largest area under dense deciduous forests. According to the India State of Forest Report, 2023, West Champaran has a total forest area of 908.23 square kilometers, of which 303.78 square kilometers are very dense forest, 527.25 square kilometres is moderately dense forest, and 77.20 square kilometres is open forest.
